target.title: feat(diagnostics-otel): add vendor-neutral session attribute option for OTel session grouping
target.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in `diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute` configuration option that exports a SHA-256 hashed session identifier as three vendor-neutral OTel span attributes on root spans, enabling session grouping across multiple observability backends (Langfuse, Latitude, Arize/Phoenix, and others).

Fixes #91927
Supersedes #92956 (closed, conflicts)

## Background

The issue originally requested `langfuse.session.id` for Langfuse session grouping. During community discussion, the Latitude team highlighted that session grouping by span attributes is a vendor-neutral convention shared across most OTLP backends. OpenClaw is already moving toward GenAI semantic conventions elsewhere in the exporter, so emitting additional vendor-neutral keys maximizes value across the ecosystem.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw redacts session keys to `"unknown"` in OTel span attributes for security. While this is a reasonable default, it makes observability backends (Langfuse, Latitude, Arize/Phoenix) unable to aggregate traces by session — the `session.id` attribute on every span is either missing or identical and meaningless. Session grouping is a core feature in every OTLP backend, and without a meaningful session identifier on root spans, users cannot group multi-turn conversations or debug session-level issues.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.base.ts` | Add `sessionAttribute?: boolean` to `DiagnosticsOtelConfig` |
| `src/config/zod-schema.ts` | Add `sessionAttribute: z.boolean().optional()` |
| `src/config/schema.help.ts` | Add help text for `diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute` |
| `src/config/schema.labels.ts` | Add field label for `diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute` |
| `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts` | Emit hashed session ID on `openclaw.run` and `openclaw.harness.run` root spans |
| `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts` | 2 test cases (enabled + disabled), 97 total passing |
| `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` | Document session attribute, privacy model, and opt-in guidance |

## Vendor-Neutral Attributes

When `sessionAttribute: true` is set, all three attributes are emitted with the same SHA-256 hash value:

- **`langfuse.session.id`** — Langfuse compatibility
- **`session.id`** — OpenInference / Arize de-facto standard
- **`gen_ai.conversation.id`** — GenAI semantic conventions

This ensures session grouping works across Langfuse, Latitude, Arize/Phoenix, and any OTLP backend without requiring backends to map non-standard keys.

## Security

- **Opt-in only** (default: `false`) — current redaction posture is unchanged
- **SHA-256 hash**, never the raw `agent:platform:peer` key
- Raw `openclaw.sessionKey` stays redacted as `"unknown"` in all existing paths
- The session identifier never leaves the box unless the operator explicitly opts in

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed:** Add opt-in `sessionAttribute` config to export hashed session identifiers on root spans.

**Real environment tested:**
- OS: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
- Runtime: Node v24.3.0, pnpm 11.2.2
- Setup: OpenClaw local dev instance, diagnostics-otel extension

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:**
1. Added `sessionAttribute?: boolean` to `DiagnosticsOtelConfig` type and Zod schema
2. On `harness.run.started` and `run.started` events, compute `crypto.createHash("sha256")` of `sessionKey` and emit three vendor-neutral attributes
3. Raw `openclaw.sessionKey` remains in the redaction set — never exposed
4. Ran reproduction script and full test suite for diagnostics-otel

**Evidence after fix (reproduction output):**
```
========================================================================
=== OpenClaw diagnostics.otel.sessionAttribute — Reproduction ===
========================================================================

--- 1. Input ---
  sessionKey:          agent:main:slack:channel:C01ABCDEFG

--- 2. SHA-256 Hash (applied in service.ts) ---
  SHA-256 hash:        6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0
  Hash length:         64 hex chars (256 bits)

--- 3. OTel Span Attributes Emitted ---
  langfuse.session.id        = 6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0
  session.id                 = 6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0
  gen_ai.conversation.id     = 6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0

--- 4. Security Verification ---
  Raw key embedded in hash?  ✅ NO
  sessionAttribute default:  false (opt-in only)
  openclaw.sessionKey:       remains redacted as "unknown"

--- 5. Root Span Attributes (OTLP format) ---
{
  "openclaw.harness.id": "codex",
  "openclaw.provider": "openai",
  "openclaw.model": "gpt-5.4",
  "openclaw.channel": "qa",
  "langfuse.session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "gen_ai.conversation.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0"
}

--- 6. Verification ---
  ✅ SHA-256 hash is irreversible — raw key not recoverable
  ✅ All three vendor-neutral attributes emitted
  ✅ sessionAttribute is opt-in (default: false)
  ✅ No raw session key in exported attributes

========================================================================
Reproduction complete — real behavior demonstrated.
```

**Test suite output:**
```
 RUN  v4.1.7 /home/0668001202/workspace/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  97 passed (97)
   Start at  12:33
   Duration  6.45s
```

**Observed result after the fix:**

Without the fix, OTel spans have no session identifier — `session.id` is missing from root spans, and backends cannot group traces by session.

With the fix and `sessionAttribute: true`:
```
root span attributes: {
  "langfuse.session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "session.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  "gen_ai.conversation.id": "6f3fa8c3356500d3642252bfad10ef1af99416a0002b3c6b19e4d453c50d3ed0",
  ...
}
```

**What was not tested:** N/A

## Tests and validation

| Test Type | Result | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Unit Tests | ✅ | 97/97 passed (2 new sessionAttribute tests) |
| Type Check | ✅ | No errors (full project `tsc --noEmit`) |

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`) — **No** (opt-in, default-off preserves existing behavior)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No` — backward compatible, `sessionAttribute` is optional with safe default `undefined`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No` — raw session key remains redacted, SHA-256 hash is irreversible, opt-in only)

What is the highest-risk area?
- The new config key is purely additive with a safe default (`undefined` = current behavior)

How is that risk mitigated?
- Default-off preserves existing behavior for all users
- Only a SHA-256 hash (not the raw key) is exported
- Full test coverage for both enabled and disabled states
- Schema help and docs explain the privacy model

target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returnscars, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a single-line backfill at the return site: `result.provider.model || resolvedModel`. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` (`"" \|\| ""` = `""`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, upstream/main

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "
import { createEmbeddingProvider } from './extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts';

// Scenario 1: Explicit model + live embedding via ZTE MaaS endpoint
const r1 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai-compatible',
  model: 'Qwen3-Embedding-8B',
  config: { models: { providers: { 'openai-compatible': { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Explicit model provider.model:', JSON.stringify(r1.provider?.model));
const vec = await r1.provider?.embedQuery?.('hello world');
console.log('embedQuery dims:', vec?.length);

// Scenario 2: No explicit model — backfill from adapter.defaultModel
const r2 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai',
  model: '',
  config: { models: { providers: { openai: { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Empty model provider.model (backfilled):', JSON.stringify(r2.provider?.model));
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Explicit model provider.model: "Qwen3-Embedding-8B"
embedQuery dims: 4096
Empty model provider.model (backfilled): "text-embedding-3-small"
```

**Observed result after fix**: Explicit model → `provider.model` matches. Empty model → `provider.model` backfilled from `adapter.defaultModel` (`"text-embedding-3-small"`). On upstream/main (without this patch), scenario 2 returns `""`.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw memory index --force` reindex through the gateway (requires full workspace setup). The proof covers the production `createEmbeddingProvider` → `embedQuery` code path with a real embedding endpoint, which is the exact code path changed by this PR.

Supersedes #91660 (31 days old, merge conflicts, larger diff with unrelated deletions). This branch is based on latest upstream/main with a focused +5/-2 diff.

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging and provider image-parsing paths, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Added `estimateBase64DecodedSize` helper that estimates decoded byte length from base64 input
- Propagated existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
- Added boundary tests for:
  - Configured limit acceptance (7MB payload under 8MB limit)
  - Over-limit rejection before decoding
  - Default limit enforcement (6 MiB)
- **No new configuration**: Uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting

## Evidence

**Environment**: macOS Vitest (Node 22.22.2)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run configured limit test
npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
✓ agents-core src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 203ms
✓ agents-support src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 184ms

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  60 passed (60)

Key test coverage:
✓ rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
✓ accepts images above MAX_IMAGE_BYTES when a higher configured maxBytes is provided
  - 7MB payload accepted under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
  - 10MB payload rejected under 8MB limit
  - 7MB payload rejected under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
```

**Configuration limit propagation verified**:
- Test file: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts:322-346`
- Scenario: 7MB payload (above default 6MiB) accepted when 8MB limit configured
- Code path: `writeCliImages` receives `maxBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024`, checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable)

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage: 60 tests across 2 test suites
- Target files: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Estimated size < maxBytes: accept
  - Estimated size > maxBytes: reject before decode
  - Configured limit > default: use configured
  - No configured limit: use default 6 MiB

target.title: fix(channels): progress drafts only for long tasks, with the model's own preamble as the status headline
target.body:
Closes #105872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes progress drafts appearing for small tasks even though the draft gate nominally waits five seconds. The second work event bypassed that delay, and the utility narrator could spend a model call before any draft was visible. Progress-mode channels also discarded the model's typed preamble even though it is the most accurate status headline available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The draft gate is now purely time-based; explicit immediate paths such as approvals and patches remain immediate. Utility narration starts only after the draft becomes visible. The shared compositor prefers fresh, typed model preambles as the headline, then uses utility narration only when the preamble is absent or stale. No config or model-facing tool surface was added.

The implementation preserves preamble item identity and retractions, counts only sanitized commentary that the compositor accepts, cancels narrator retries and expiry timers when a turn settles, rejects stale in-flight utility results, resets queued-turn lifecycle state, and refreshes same-text headlines when a new preamble item arrives.

Maintainer decision: the three additive optional Plugin SDK progress-lifecycle fields are accepted as the canonical channel-owned seam. They keep transport presentation ownership outside the core agent loop while preserving a typed, upgrade-safe contract.

## User Impact

- Fast turns produce only the final answer: no transient draft, receipt, or utility narration call.
- Long turns show the model's current preamble as the status headline, with utility narration filling genuine silences and tool activity retained below it.
- Retractions clear the matching headline, final delivery removes the draft, and queued turns begin with fresh lifecycle state.

## Evidence

- Frozen reviewed head: `3c2bfbde13b6498614fe5fe48cd35f45756869f6`, rebased onto `78305b65b1da0d874a2767f7ff936a696eadf936`.
- Exact-head Blacksmith Testbox lease `tbx_01kxezbvj63sae10n4jzxe9c1j`; hydration/run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29295192643.
- All ten touched test files passed: 1,081 tests across plugin SDK, auto-reply, Discord, Telegram, Matrix, Teams, Slack, and the shared compositor.
- Hosted CI found one stale generated docs-map heading after the docs rename; `docs/docs_map.md` is regenerated and `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` passes on the final head.
- Exact hosted CI has one unrelated current-main deadcode failure for two exports under `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/**`; this PR does not touch `src/agents/**`.
- Fresh autoreview found and drove same-text/new-item freshness and queued-turn request-context repairs; focused follow-up review returned no accepted or actionable findings.
- Hosted CI exposed a plugin boundary contract gap. The follow-up exports the channel-owned progress lifecycle options through `GetReplyOptions`; exact-head `pnpm tsgo:prod`, all 121 extension package boundary compiles, the plugin SDK API baseline, and a fresh autoreview are green.
- Direct Codex protocol contract checked: `../codex/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs` defines commentary/final message phases; `../codex/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs` carries agent-message `id`, `text`, and `phase`; `../codex/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs` maps content deltas to agent-message deltas.
- Exact-head native Telegram Desktop comparison passed at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29295448822 for candidate `3c2bfbde13b6498614fe5fe48cd35f45756869f6`; published GIF/MP4 evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106026#issuecomment-4963961198. Discord uses the same compositor and settlement lifecycle, with 131 focused Discord tests in the exact-head run.

target.title: Add CLAW.md manifest support
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `CLAW.md` as a human-readable Claw manifest format. YAML frontmatter is normalized through the same typed manifest schema as JSON; the Markdown body is documentation only.

- package directories may point `package.json#openclaw.claw` at `CLAW.md`
- standalone and feed-resolved `CLAW.md` sources use the same parser and structured diagnostics
- `claws export` now emits `package.json`, `CLAW.md`, and managed workspace sidecars
- malformed frontmatter, including unresolved YAML aliases, fails as diagnostics rather than throwing

This is an OpenClaw compatibility slice above #102982. It does not define the future harness-agnostic `npx claws` specification; it makes the current OpenClaw package format easier to inspect and author while preserving the existing lifecycle contract.

RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
Depends on: #102982

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/feed.test.ts src/claws/export.test.ts src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts` (67 passed)
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/claws/reader.ts src/claws/feed.ts src/claws/export.ts src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/feed.test.ts src/claws/export.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs`
- `codex review --uncommitted` (no actionable correctness regression)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` remains blocked by the inherited unused import in `src/claws/package-update.ts` (`PersistedClawPackageRef`, TS6133), present in the base commit.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
A human-authored or exported `CLAW.md` package must inspect and add through the normal consented Claw lifecycle, including feed resolution.

Real environment tested:
WSL Ubuntu 24.04, this branch, local OpenClaw CLI with `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` and bundled plugins disabled.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Created a temporary package containing `package.json` with `openclaw.claw: "CLAW.md"` and a typed YAML-frontmatter manifest.
2. Ran `node --import tsx src/entry.ts claws inspect <package> --json`.
3. Ran `node --import tsx src/entry.ts claws add <package> --yes --json`.
4. Ran the full exported-package inspect/add lifecycle E2E and feed-resolution tests.

Evidence after fix:
`inspect` returned `valid: true`, package identity `@example/briefing@1.0.0`, and manifest path ending in `CLAW.md`. `add --yes` returned `status: "complete"` with final agent id `briefing`. The focused suite passed 67 tests.

Observed result after fix:
The same typed manifest works when read directly, through a package directory, through a local feed, and after `claws export`; it retains existing plan, consent, provenance, and lifecycle behavior.

What was not tested:
No external registry/ClawHub fetch or non-OpenClaw harness adapter; this PR is local OpenClaw format compatibility only.

target.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a restricted agent could create a recurring cron job with a trigger script and a `systemEvent` payload, then have that script receive the full coding tool surface. Main-session cron jobs require `systemEvent`, so the common path bypassed the creator's tool policy whenever cron triggers were enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator tool cap now applies whenever a cron job has a trigger script, in addition to isolated `agentTurn` jobs. The cap is retained on every cron payload shape, survives updates, is persisted through the cron SQLite store so it survives a gateway restart, and is passed to the headless trigger evaluator. This keeps the existing agent-turn behavior while covering main-session system events and command payloads.

Distinct from #12736, which concerns global cron deny policy; #97317 and #101349, which concern isolated agent-turn defaults; and #41484, which concerns elevated execution scope.

## User Impact

Agents restricted to a small tool set can use cron triggers without acquiring shell, exec, or patch capabilities beyond that set. Existing unrestricted operator-created cron jobs continue to work with their configured policy.

## Rebase onto current main

This branch was rebased onto current `main`. Three things needed re-expressing against main's current code, none of which change the fix:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` conflicted because `main` replaced `Type.Object({...}, { additionalProperties: false })` with the `closedObject()` helper. The cap fields were re-expressed in that helper form.
- The changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet that landed on `main` in #106387 forbids an already-oversized file from growing. `src/cron/service/jobs.ts`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` are all over the limit, so the cap additions tripped the gate. Cohesive declarations were hoisted into three companion leaf modules, mirroring the existing sibling convention: `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.types.ts` (type-only), `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.types.ts` (type-only wire types), and `src/cron/service/payload-merge.ts` (the cron payload merge rules the patch touches). All three source files are now back at or below their baseline line counts and the ratchet passes.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` now uses the repo's `expectDefined` helper for indexed job access, which main's tightened unchecked index access requires.

## Evidence

- The touched suites were re-run after the rebase with `node scripts/test-projects.mjs` and all pass: 145 checks in `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`, 199 checks across `src/cron/normalize.test.ts`, `src/cron/store.test.ts`, `src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts` and `src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts`, and 23 checks in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/cron-validators.test.ts`. 367 checks total.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` restart-aware round-trip coverage for the `systemEvent` and `command` tool caps; both fail on the pre-persistence codec and pass here.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` both pass, `node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` passes, and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files is clean.
- An earlier restart cap-loss and reload proof, pinned to a previous head, is in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104430#issuecomment-4945702410

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A cron trigger script created by a restricted caller must not receive tools the caller cannot use; a `systemEvent` main-session job with a trigger script previously kept no tool cap.
Real environment tested: The production `createCronTool` entry point (`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts`) driven via `tool.execute("add", ...)` on pristine main `1708faf85b` and on PR head `c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b` with the identical restricted creator (`creatorToolAllowlist: ["read", "cron"]`) creating a trigger-script `systemEvent` job; only the gateway RPC boundary was replaced to capture the params the tool sends.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PROOF_OUT=/tmp/proof-after.txt node_modules/.bin/tsx cron-trigger-proof.ts` (harness invokes the real cron tool `add` with `trigger.script` + `payload.kind=systemEvent`, prints the captured `cron.add` payload)
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 1708faf85b, identical restricted-caller input)
{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed"}
# AFTER (this patch, head c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b, identical input)
{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed","toolsAllow":["read","cron"]}
```
Observed result after fix: The persisted trigger-script job carries `toolsAllow: ["read","cron"]`, capping the trigger to exactly the creator-visible tools instead of receiving the full coding tool surface.
What was not tested: No live gateway tick with a provider-backed trigger evaluation, and the full build was not run.

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from successful `users.info` calls but had no pruning — every unique user ID accumulated forever. `channelCache` already bounds at 1024 via `pruneMapToMaxSize`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the current-main `channelCache` pattern for users: LRU touch on read, `pruneMapToMaxSize` on write, cap `SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 2048`, using `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`.

## User Impact

- Long-running Slack monitors no longer retain unbounded user-name cache entries.
- Active users stay resident (LRU touch); oldest entries evict first after the cap.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `fdfd1de35efcefb066ea71e0775b763cbe3aae0c` (rebased onto current `main`)


### Rank-up refresh (fdfd1de35efc)
- Rebased onto current `main` `345083a5ab95` (single commit, parents=main).
- Local pre-push: `oxfmt --check` + `oxlint` + `vitest` on touched Slack monitor files — green (27 tests across both PR surfaces).
- **Credential rotation:** Slack bot/user/app tokens used in earlier proof pastes must be rotated by the operator; agent cannot rotate workspace secrets.


### CI fix (head `fdfd1de3…`)

- Extracted shared `readLruMapEntry` / `writeLruMapEntry` to `extensions/slack/src/monitor/lru-map-cache.ts` so oversized `context.ts` **shrinks** (818→789; LOC ratchet base was 801).
- Removed broken unused `readCachedUser` (infinite self-call); user reads now use `readLruMapEntry(userCache, …)` so LRU recency tests match production.

### Rank-up coverage

| Rank-up | Status |
|---|---|
| Rebase onto current main | done |
| Supported `pruneMapToMaxSize` (same as channelCache) | done |
| Eviction + LRU-recency unit coverage | done |

| Rotate previously exposed credentials | caller re-issued tokens for this proof; **rotate again after paste into chat** |

target.title: fix(slack): mark connected status degraded without bot identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Slack `auth.test` fails at boot, or `channels.slack.botToken` is actually a user token (`xoxp` with `user_id` but no `bot_id`), Socket Mode can still connect while main previously published `healthState: "healthy"`. Operators see a connected channel while mention detection is disabled and required-mention rooms fail closed — silent inbound loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transport liveness (`connected: true`) remains useful, but advertising `healthy` is wrong when bot identity is missing under the current bot_id-gated contract (`botUserId = botId ? authUserId : ""`). Publish `healthState: "degraded"` with `lastError`, and log `slack socket mode connected (degraded identity)`.

## User Impact

- Misconfigured bot tokens / failed `auth.test` no longer look healthy in channel status.
- Valid bot-token installs stay `healthy` on connect.
- App Home slash-command wiring and allowlist-resolution formatting are untouched.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `1ccda079b24fc46ecbfe10a23bbec29dde145b03`


### Rank-up refresh (1ccda079b24f)
- Rebased onto current `main` `345083a5ab95` (single commit, parents=main).
- Local pre-push: `oxfmt --check` + `oxlint` + `vitest` on touched Slack monitor files — green (27 tests across both PR surfaces).
- **Credential rotation:** Slack bot/user/app tokens used in earlier proof pastes must be rotated by the operator; agent cannot rotate workspace secrets.

### Rank-up coverage

| Rank-up | Status |
|---|---|
| Real Socket Mode startup proof (healthy + degraded) via `@slack/bolt` `app.start()` + patched `publishSlackConnectedStatus` / runtime logs | done — redacted transcript below |
| Fix `check-test-types` (`bot_id: undefined` → `never.trim`) | done — optional `bot_id?: string` fixture; omit property |
| Rotate pasted Slack credentials | **please rotate** `xoxb` / `xoxp` / `xapp` used for proof |

### L1 unit (provider-path)

- `marks socket mode degraded when boot identity is unavailable`
- `marks socket mode degraded for user_id without bot_id (bot-gated contract)` — typed as `{ user_id: string; bot_id?: string }` so `check-test-types` stays green

### L3 live Socket Mode startup (redacted) — 2026-07-13

Real `@slack/bolt` Socket Mode `App({ token, appToken, socketMode: true }).start()`, then the same identity gate + `publishSlackConnectedStatus` / runtime log contract used by patched `onStarted`. Tokens never printed (kind + last-6 only). **Rotate bot / user / app-level tokens — they were pasted into chat.**

```text
# Slack Socket Mode status proof — PR #105556
Time (UTC): 2026-07-13T16:23:03.567Z
Tokens never printed; kind + last-6 only. IDs redacted.

{
  "note": "Real @slack/bolt Socket Mode app.start() + patched publishSlackConnectedStatus onStarted contract",
  "token_kinds": { "bot": "xoxb-…109Tev", "user": "xoxp-…b4311c", "app": "xapp-…733989" },
  "results": [
    {
      "label": "A healthy bot token + app token (Socket Mode)",
      "ok": true,
      "authRaw": { "ok": true, "has_user_id": true, "has_bot_id": true },
      "identityDegraded": false,
      "statuses": [{ "connected": true, "healthState": "healthy", "lastError": null }],
      "logs": [
        "setStatus {\"connected\":true,\"healthState\":\"healthy\",\"lastError\":null}",
        "slack socket mode connected"
      ]
    },
    {
      "label": "B user token misused as botToken + app token (Socket Mode degraded)",
      "ok": true,
      "authRaw": { "ok": true, "has_user_id": true, "has_bot_id": false },
      "identityDegraded": true,

        "connected": true,

}
```

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.

    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 127      description:
 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: fix(web): apply Control UI text size to content typography
target.body:
## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

## Validation

- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRTUXB | tr '\n' ' ')`
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run ui/src/components/form-controls.browser.test.ts ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts ui/src/pages/config/view.browser.test.ts ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts`

- Playwright screenshot proof against the local mock server for Settings at M, Overview/Channels at XXL, and mobile Overview at XXL.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
